league_wrap.title: Camp Desk — Wednesday, Aug 12
league_wrap.bottom_line: Minnesota named a starter. Most other camps are still availability, rotation, or preseason scripts — not a reason to invent a lean. Thin info stays Pass.
storylines: Vikings: Kevin O’Connell named Kyler Murray the starter Tuesday after 10 camp practices. J.J. McCarthy is the No. 2. That is a real depth-chart change — flag it for the source-of-truth job; do not rewrite the Model from this note.

Falcons: Still not a grass derby. Michael Penix Jr. is not cleared for 11-on-11s (ACL rehab; late-August window). Tua Tagovailoa’s back issue paused his sample. Cooper Rush is a camp arm, not a Week 1 lean.

Browns: Todd Monken is still splitting first-team reps. Each of Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders is slated to start one of the first two preseason games. Spencer Fano moved to left tackle with the ones — OL, not a QB crown.

Giants: Jaxson Dart’s second camp is uneven in a new under-center offense (Matt Nagy / John Harbaugh). Tuesday was the 12th practice; Saturday’s preseason opener vs Minnesota is the next public tape, not a starter vote.

Packers: Javon Bullard sat Monday with a foot bruise (same foot as prior surgery). Corner mix is fluid (Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Benjamin St-Juste). Matt LaFleur wants some starter preseason snaps — amount TBD.
Steelers: Aaron Rodgers is locked as Week 1 QB1. Mason Rudolph has the twos. Backup math is the camp story, not a Rodgers lean.
Bengals: WR3 behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is the live battle — Andrei Iosivas projected, Colbie Young pushing. Joe Burrow being full-go does not mint a WR3 ticket.
Jets: Brandon Stephens is one starting corner. The other side is Nahshon Wright vs Azareye’h Thomas — too close for a depth rewrite.
league_wrap.what_to_watch: Preseason openers this weekend (Browns at Chicago Saturday; Giants vs Vikings Saturday) are evaluation tape, not market permission.

sources.label: Andrew Krammer, Star Tribune (Murray named starter)

team_notes.title: Vikings camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: Murray is the named starter after 10 practices. McCarthy is the backup. Pass on manufacturing a new win-total lean from the presser alone.
key_points: O’Connell cited command and high-completion days, including an Aug. 1 first-team period (8-for-8, five to Justin Jefferson).
Murray’s first practice as the starter: 15-of-16 in 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 (Star Tribune). Two interceptions at Sunday’s TCO night practice are still on the tape.
McCarthy “absolutely” has a future here, per O’Connell — immediate-response backup, not a buried prospect.
team_notes.what_to_watch: Does the ones-only install stay clean against Flores’ looks before the Giants preseason game?
team_notes.sot_flag: Named QB1. Queue the existing SoT/depth job — do not publish a new active_run from this prose.

team_notes.title: Falcons camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: Still no real QB competition on the grass. Availability is the story. Week 1 starter lean stays Pass.
key_points: Penix is not cleared for full team 11-on-11s; he has described a roughly four-week window to the next rehab stage (late August / missing most of the preseason if that holds).
Tagovailoa’s tight back kept him out of early 11s; Stefanski and ESPN framed it as short-term, not a season event.
Cooper Rush was signed so camp had a veteran arm next to UDFA Jack Strand — camp body, not a futures ticket.
team_notes.what_to_watch: First multi-day padded 11-on-11 sample from either Tua or Penix.
team_notes.sot_flag: Dual-QB availability still unresolved. Flag for SoT; do not crown a starter from camp fog.

team_notes.title: Browns camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: The QB job is still a split. Monken said he will tell you when he knows. One Saturday audible is not a crown.
key_points: Aug. 10: still a competition; each of Watson and Sanders starts one of the first two preseason games (Chicago Aug. 15, Buffalo Aug. 22).
Aug. 8: Monken said Sanders would take the ones, then Watson took every first-team rep — staff said personnel groupings, not a naming.
Confirmed depth move: Spencer Fano to left tackle with the ones. That is OL, not QB1.
team_notes.what_to_watch: Who actually starts Saturday in Chicago — and whether the other gets Buffalo.
team_notes.sot_flag: Fano to LT1 is a depth input for the SoT job. QB1 still unset — do not invent a starter.

team_notes.title: Giants camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: Dart is the starter working through a new offense. Uneven camp is process, not a benching rumor. Pass on a Dart lean from one bad Tuesday.
key_points: Tuesday was practice 12 of Harbaugh’s first camp. Nagy’s install is still midstream and asks Dart to live under center more than last year.
Coaches described the hurdle as getting his eyes to the right spot in the progression — filter the playbook to what he executes.
Two practices left before Saturday’s home preseason opener against Minnesota.
team_notes.what_to_watch: Clean first-team script vs Minnesota, not a single 7-on-7 period.

team_notes.title: Packers camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: Monday’s notes are availability and a fluid corner mix. Unofficial depth chart ≠ locked Week 1. Pass.
key_points: Javon Bullard sat with a foot bruise he called not overly concerning; Kitan Oladapo took slot snaps with the ones.
Corner pairs rotated: Nixon/Cisse and Cisse/St-Juste. Carrington Valentine has been out with a leg injury (SI / unofficial chart context).
LaFleur wants healthy starters to play some preseason; volume and which game TBD. Edgerrin Cooper (foot) returned Monday.
team_notes.what_to_watch: Whether Bullard practices this week and which corner pair survives the first preseason script vs Pittsburgh.

team_notes.title: Bengals camp — Aug 12
team_notes.bottom_line: WR3 is a real camp battle. Chase and Higgins are the constants. No tag from a strong Iosivas week.
key_points: Andrei Iosivas is the projected third receiver; fourth-rounder Colbie Young is in the first-team mix (Ben Baby, ESPN).
Iosivas’s 2025 scoring rate dipped (two of 12 career TDs last year). Burrow at full strength is the volume backdrop, not a WR3 lock.
Three-receiver personnel is the snap that matters — not a camp one-hander.
team_notes.what_to_watch: Who lines up as the Z/slot with the ones in the first preseason script.
